```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library("naboer")
have_ape <- requireNamespace("ape", quietly = TRUE)
have_rsample <- requireNamespace("rsample", quietly = TRUE)
```

Validation should reflect the ecological prediction task. Predicting another
observation at a sampled station differs from predicting a new station, an
unfamiliar environment or an unobserved taxon. Dependence buffers address the
relationship between held-out and training observations; whole-group holdouts
also change which observational units are available to the model.

This article uses a small monitoring dataset with repeated observations from six
stations in two networks. All examples preserve its original observation order.

```{r}
observations <- tibble::tibble(
  observation = seq_len(24),
  network = rep(c("north", "south"), each = 12),
  station = rep(paste0("station", seq_len(6)), each = 4),
  date = rep(as.Date("2025-05-01") + 0:3, 6),
  temperature = rep(c(4, 6, 12, 14, 20, 22), each = 4),
  moisture = rep(c(90, 85, 65, 60, 35, 30), each = 4),
  habitat = rep(c("wet", "wet", "intermediate", "intermediate", "dry", "dry"), each = 4)
)
```

## Whole stations and hierarchical groups

Leave one station out to assess predictions at stations unavailable during
fitting. Select all identifying levels when station labels are only unique
within a network. The combination of the selected columns defines a group.

```{r}
new_station <- observations |>
  group_folds(group = c(network, station), id = observation)
tibble::as_tibble(new_station)
assessment_indices(new_station, folds = 1)
```

For V-fold CV, whole groups can be allocated together. With `balance = TRUE`,
allocation aims to balance observation counts rather than the number of groups.
The local seed makes allocation reproducible and preserves the caller's random
number state.

```{r}
station_vfold <- observations |>
  group_folds(group = c(network, station), v = 3, balance = TRUE, seed = 21)
tibble::as_tibble(station_vfold)
```

Use `.by = network` when networks define independent dependence domains. A
constructor then treats a station in one network as distinct from a station
with the same label in another. V-fold allocation may score groups from several
domains in the same fold; it never splits a group. Choose `group = network` to
hold out an entire network instead.

## New environmental conditions

Environmental folds hold out clusters of observations in selected predictor
space. Numeric predictors are standardised by default before seeded k-means
clustering. Here temperature and moisture have different scales, so
standardisation gives both an equal role in the distance calculation.

```{r}
new_environment <- observations |>
  environmental_folds(predictors = c(temperature, moisture), v = 3, seed = 22)
tibble::as_tibble(new_environment)
```

Clustering uses the selected predictors, so its interpretation depends on that
selection. Missing or nonfinite predictors cause an error. Predictors constant
within a domain are reported and excluded; an entirely constant domain cannot
be clustered. With `.by`, each domain is clustered separately.

Existing scientific strata can be more useful than data-derived clusters.
Supply `strata` instead of `predictors` to leave each stratum out. An optional
`v` allocates whole strata to fewer folds.

```{r}
new_habitat <- observations |>
  environmental_folds(strata = habitat)
tibble::as_tibble(new_habitat)
```

Environmental holdouts may involve extrapolation. Their errors answer a different
question from random V-fold errors, even when both use the same model and data.

## Phylogenetic dependence and new taxa

The following examples require the optional **ape** package. Their chunks run
only when `requireNamespace("ape", quietly = TRUE)` succeeds. Install ape to
execute the tree examples locally; the other examples do not need it.

```{r phylogeny, eval=have_ape}
tree <- ape::read.tree(
  text = "((oak:1,beech:1):2,(pine:1,fir:1):2);"
)
taxon_data <- tibble::tibble(
  observation = seq_len(24),
  taxon = rep(c("oak", "beech", "pine", "fir"), each = 6),
  response = seq_len(24)
)

near_taxa <- taxon_data |>
  neighbourhoods(
    phylogenetic = phylogenetic_window(tree, taxon, radius = 2),
    id = observation
  )
tibble::as_tibble(near_taxa, folds = c(1, 13), membership = TRUE)
```

The radius uses branch-length units and includes its boundary. In this tree,
oak and beech are two units apart, while oak and pine are six units apart.
Each focal observation omits all observations of its own taxon and nearby taxa
in its domain. Tree distances are calculated among unique observed taxa, then
mapped to observation rows; replicated taxa do not enlarge the distance matrix.
Unused tree tips are allowed, but every observed taxon must match a tip label.
Every branch needs a finite, nonnegative length.

For new-taxon prediction, complete-linkage clustering produces blocks of taxa.
Choose either a number of clusters with `v`, or a distance threshold with
`height`. Replicated observations of a taxon stay together.

```{r phylogenetic-blocks, eval=have_ape}
taxon_blocks <- taxon_data |>
  phylogenetic_folds(tree, taxon, height = 2)
tibble::as_tibble(taxon_blocks)
```

Alternatively, select scientifically meaningful clades explicitly. The tree
must be rooted, and the selected nonoverlapping clades must cover every observed
taxon. Supply complete descendant tip sets or tree-node numbers. Arbitrary tip
sets that do not form a complete clade are rejected.

```{r phylogenetic-clades, eval=have_ape}
new_clade <- taxon_data |>
  phylogenetic_folds(
    tree, taxon,
    clades = list(c("oak", "beech"), c("pine", "fir"))
  )
tibble::as_tibble(new_clade, membership = TRUE)
```

## Buffered resampling and rsample

Start with a focal assessment design and add a one-day exclusion buffer within
each station. This changes omission membership while retaining the assessment
observations that contribute to the criterion. Buffers expand from assessment
observations only; they do not expand recursively from other buffer rows.

```{r buffered-design}
buffered <- observations |>
  loo_folds(id = observation) |>
  buffer_folds(
    temporal = temporal_window(time_span(1, "days")),
    key = station, index = date, within = "key"
  )
tibble::as_tibble(buffered, folds = 2, membership = TRUE)
analysis_indices(buffered, folds = 2)
```

The next chunk requires optional **rsample** and is skipped when it is unavailable.
The exported manual resamples preserve analysis and assessment independently.
Buffer-only observations belong to neither set. On import, omission is the
complement of analysis, so those observations remain excluded.

```{r rsample-roundtrip, eval=have_rsample}
resamples <- as_rset(buffered)
restored <- from_rset(resamples, id = observation)
identical(assessment_indices(restored), assessment_indices(buffered))
identical(omission_indices(restored), omission_indices(buffered))
identical(analysis_indices(restored), analysis_indices(buffered))
```

Ordinary rsample V-fold and repeated assessment designs can be imported.
Bootstrap analysis samples containing duplicated rows cannot be expressed by
an omission set and are rejected. All splits must refer to identical data in
the same order.

Finally, export the design for mgcv with `as_nei(buffered)`, and fit against
`fold_data(buffered)`. Construct folds after preparing complete modelling data
and use `na.action = stats::na.fail` when fitting. A valid design still requires
checking whether the NCV approximation is accurate for the intended model and
omission size.
